authors: Peter Hondelmann, Christina Paul, Monika Schreiner, Rainer Meyhöfer
name: luh-importance-of-antixenosis-and-antibiosis-resistance-whitefly-brussels-sprouts
notes:
The data are parts of the BSc-Thesis of Christina Paul Gartenbauwissenschaften) with the title: 
"Resistenzpotential verschiedener Rosenkohlsorten (Brassica oleracea L. var. gemmifera DC.) gegenüber der Kohlmottenschildlaus Aleyrodes proletella (L.) (Hemiptera: Aleyrodidae)" from 2014
and her MSc-Thesis "Untersuchungen zu Resistenzmechanismen von Rosenkohl (Brassica oleracea L. var. gemmifera DC.) gegenüber der Kohlmottenschildlaus Aleyrodes proletella (L.) (Hemiptera: Aleyrodidae)" 
from 2017 at Institute of Horticultural production Systems, Sec. Phytomedicine. 

The data were also collected for the project "Neue Ansätze zur Bekämpfung der Kohlmottenschildlaus (Aleyrodes proletella) einem Problemschädling im Kohlanbau" and are partly published in the final report of the project (https://orgprints.org/32012/1/32012-12NA022-luh-meyhoefer-2016-bekaempfung-kohlmottenschildlaus.pdf). The project was funded by BLE in context of "Bundesprogramm Ökologischer Landbau und andere Formen nachhaltiger Landwirtschaft", grant number: 2812NA022.

All data are published 2019/2020 in the journal Insects 2020, 11, 56; https://doi.org/10.3390/insects11010056

Detailed methods of data collection and analyses are desribed in the paper and final report as mentioned above. 
The files were created by MS Excel 2016.
title: Importance of Antixenosis and Antibiosis Resistance to the Cabbage Whitefly (Aleyrodes proletella) in Brussels Sprout Cultivars

resources.description: Data on infestation of 16 Brussels sprout cultivars by adult A. proletella (Hemiptera: Aleyrodidae) in three choice experiments with circular design in a greenhouse.
resources.name: Choice experiments (antixenosis)

resources.description: Cabbage whitefly antibiosis results (offspring mortality, fecundity (number of eggs per day and female) and estimated degree of soiling caused by CWF infestation (due to honeydew, sooty moulds, exuviae, etc.) of the field trial.
resources.name: field trial antibiosis

resources.description: Development of A. proletella on different Brussel sprout cultivars in a field trial on the university campus (52°23'39.4" N, 9°42'13.3" E, Germany) with six cultivars and four blocks per cultivar. Plots were arranged in a completely randomised block design in two rows (24 plots in total) and had a size of 13 m2 with 36 plants each. Infestation was recorded biweekly with counting egg clutches, larvae and adults on 10 plants (except plants at the edge) in every plot.
resources.name: field trial antixenosis

resources.description: concentrations (µmol/g dry mass) of  glucosinolates and main glucosinolate groups (indole, alkenyl & methylsulfinyl GS) of five Brussels sprout cultivars at two leaf levels
resources.name: Glucosinolates

resources.description: Results of antibiosis experiments including developmental time (egg to adult),  weight (hatched adults),  of cabbage whiteflies (A. proletella) after development on different Brussels sprout cultivars in a climate chamber at 21 ± 2 °C, 55% rH, 16:8 L:D.
resources.name: No–choice experiments (antibiosis)1

resources.description: Results of antibiosis experiments including mortality (combined egg and larval), fecundity rate (number of eggs per day and female), life–time fertility (number of offspring per female over whole lifetime), and longevity of females of cabbage whiteflies (A. proletella) after development on different Brussels sprout cultivars in a climate chamber at 21 ± 2 °C, 55% rH, 16:8 L:D.
resources.name: No–choice experiments (antibiosis)2
